newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTOR RACING-BERGER GRABS POLE FOR GERMAN GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BERGER GRABS POLE FOR GERMAN GRAND PRIX.

text.p: Austrian Gerhard Berger returned to competition with a vengeance on Saturday when he grabbed pole position for Sunday's German Grand Prix.

The 37-year-old driver, who had missed the last three races following sinus surgery and during that time also suffered the loss of his father who was killed in an air crash, stunned a huge crowd at the high-speed Hockenheim track south of Heidelberg by clocking the fastest time in his Renault-powered car.
Two days after announcing he would not be driving for the Benetton team next season, Berger's display was a perfect shop-window demonstration of his talent and experience.
He was 0.023 seconds faster than nearest rival Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Peugeot-powered Jordan, with Finland's Mika Hakkinen in a McLaren, powered by Mercedes-Benz, third.
It was the first pole position for Benetton since Germany's Michael Schumacher left the team in 1995.
Double world champion and current series leader Schumacher was fourth fastest in Ferrari just ahead of Germany's third driver in the event, Heinz-Harald Frentzen in a Williams Renault who was fifth.
Schumacher's 22-year-old younger brother Ralf, in the second Jordan, was seventh behind Frenchman Jean Alesi in the second Benetton. Alesi was sixth.
World champion Damon Hill of Britain was a creditable 13th in his Yamaha-powered Arrows car on a circuit where outright speed and engine strength matter more than anywhere else.

Berger's pole position was his first since the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa-Francorchamps in 1995 -- 32 races ago. It was also the 12th pole of his career on the eve of his 203rd Grand Prix and a performance which gave him a perfect opportunity to make up for his disappointment in last year's race when his engine failed while he was leading with only one lap remaining.
